title: Swap the toner cartridge in a desktop laser printer and shut its door
instruction: Replace the toner cartridge in the printer with the new one from the table, put the old one down on the table, and shut the printer's front door. Don't touch the black roller inside the printer.
context: Changing a laser printer's toner is one of the most common pieces of office and home upkeep. The cartridge is a 34 cm long, 0.6-0.7 kg block held by one handle; it has to come out and go in square along the bay's two guide rails, its side bosses must drop into the seat notches at their end, and the door only shuts on a seated cartridge. Touching the transfer roller leaves marks on every later print.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Printer: a compact monochrome desktop laser printer, light grey ABS, 40 cm wide, 36 cm deep, 23 cm tall, 7.5 kg, on four 3 x 3 cm rubber feet (friction about 0.9 on the table), standing free (not fixed) and square to the robot, its front face at x = 0.27, centred on y = 0. Its toner bay is open at the front between the side walls (37 cm wide, from 5 cm to 21.5 cm high) and at the front 11 cm of its top. Front door: an L-shaped grey ABS cover, 350 g, 36.6 cm wide, 1.2 cm thick: a front panel 16.3 cm tall and a top flange 10.7 cm deep, with a 2 x 0.8 cm rib along the inside of the panel near its top. It is hinged along the bay's bottom front edge (5.5 cm high), swings toward the robot with stops at shut and 80 degrees, and starts fully open (80 degrees). Shut, its weight is behind the hinge and holds it shut; open past about 12 degrees, it falls open. Inside the bay, on each side wall: a dark grey guide rail pair (lower and upper rail, 8 mm thick, 9 mm out from the wall) sloping down 15 degrees toward the back from 1.7 cm behind the front face to 9.5 cm behind it, the slot between them 16 mm tall on the right and 24 mm on the left, with 8 mm lead-in flares; behind each rail a seat notch 14 mm long and 12 mm deeper than the rail's end (notch floor 10.5 cm high), closed by a back stop, with the slot's ceiling running on flat over the notch to the back stop, so a boss can reach its notch only along its slot. Two support ribs on the bay floor (4 cm wide, centred 11 cm either side of the middle, 2.2 to 4 cm behind the front face, 1.45 cm tall) carry the seated cartridge's front. A black transfer roller (12 mm diameter, 30 cm long) lies across the bay floor 6 cm behind the front face, its top 4 mm above the floor. Toner cartridges (two, the same shape): a black plastic body 34 cm long (along y), 10 cm deep, 9 cm tall; on top in the middle a handle 4 cm long (along x), 1.6 cm thick and 4.5 cm tall; on each end, 3.5 cm behind the body's centre, a side boss standing out 13.5 mm (1.5 mm from the bay wall), 10 mm long and 10 mm tall on the right end, 18 mm tall on the left (the keying: turned around, it does not fit the rails). The old cartridge (grey handle, 0.55 kg) starts seated in the printer: bosses down in the notches, body centred at (0.337, 0), bottom 6.5 cm high, front face 5 mm behind the shut door's inside. The new cartridge (orange handle, 0.70 kg) lies upright on the table, square to the printer, centred at (0.205, -0.40). The table left of the printer (around (0.205, 0.40)) is clear. Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time: the printer is moved more than 1 cm or turned or tipped more than 2 degrees from its taped outline; any part of either arm touches the transfer roller; a cartridge that no gripper holds falls faster than 0.5 m/s (a free fall of about 1.3 cm; sliding down the rails is not a fall); a cartridge tilts more than 30 degrees; or a cartridge leaves the table. Otherwise, at the end (seating, footprint and door are measured relative to the printer): 0.2 if the old cartridge is wholly outside the printer's footprint, resting on the table (lowest corner within 8 mm of it, level within 5 degrees) and let go; 0.5 if, as well, the new cartridge is seated (both bosses down in the notches: body within 4 mm of its seated position, level and square within 2 degrees) and let go; 0.75 if, as well, the door is shut (within 2 degrees, the top of its front panel within 6 mm of the case front). 1.0 (success, held for 1 s): all of that, with every part of both arms at least 3 cm from the door and both cartridges and the cartridges and door still. Let go means no gripper is closed on the handle. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0.
reset_notes: Put the old cartridge back: slide it in along the rails and lower its bosses into the notches. Put the new one back upright at its mark on the table, open the door to its 80-degree stop, and check the printer is inside its taped outline. Use dummy cartridges (empty shells weighted to 0.55 and 0.70 kg) so no toner can spill; the printer stays unplugged.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Printer is a free articulation on rubber feet (friction 0.9); case, rails and door are ABS (0.3); its door hinge is lightly damped, with stops at 0 and 80 degrees and no latch, held shut by its own weight. Rails, notches and bosses are boxes with 3 mm play; the transfer roller is a fixed cylinder. Contacts (roller, arm clearance, holding) are judged from link positions as capsules, like a video check. No toner, springs or electronics are simulated.
